clue.text: So unlike the minister, backing collective

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word for a non-cleric is read from its end

parts.note: laic means lay, not of the clergy, so unlike a minister of religion

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a group differs from a churchman yet supports it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns LAIC into CIAL, which follows SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Social and collective both describe things done by a community or group together.

clue.text: Barman's assistant?

parts.note: reads as a pub helper, but the bar is the legal profession and the barman a barrister, whose instructions come from this lawyer

explanation.definitionFit: In England a solicitor prepares cases and briefs barristers, members of the Bar.

clue.text: Secret lore putting learner among top marks?

indicators.note: among says the learner goes in the middle of the string of grades

parts.note: a run of high grades C, A, B, B, A, A, all from the top of the scale
L is a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Mysterious teaching that lands a pupil among the best grades.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that 'top marks' is loose: a string of top-end letter grades, CABBAA, with L set among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabbala is a body of mystical Jewish teaching, hence esoteric knowledge.

clue.text: Lacking any distinction, nevertheless

definitions.meaning: with nothing to tell things apart, identical

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means identical in one sense and serves as an adverb meaning even so in the other.

clue.text: Rascal, a waggish type found here

definitions.text: Rascal, a waggish type found here

indicators.note: the clue says the word is to be found here, in its own letters, running across the opening words

explanation.surface: A mischievous joker can be spotted in this very sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'raSCAL A WAGgish'; the whole clue doubles as the definition, since a scalawag is a rascal and a joker.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalawag is an old word for a scamp or rogue, a mischief-maker.

clue.text: Provision for Head in which one's soundly beaten

definitions.meaning: a piece of headgear, with Head dressed up as a title
the idiom knocked into a three-cornered hat means thoroughly defeated

explanation.definitionFit: A cocked hat is a three-cornered hat, and 'knock into a cocked hat' is an idiom for trounce.

clue.text: Instrument another's not following initially

indicators.note: not says the letter that follows is missing from the other instrument

parts.note: another is another instrument, a flute

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of the word following

explanation.surface: One musical instrument declines to come in behind another at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is a second instrument, FLUTE; 'not' removes F, the first letter of 'following'.
explanation.definitionFit: The lute is a plucked stringed instrument with a rounded back.

clue.text: Statesman taking over command post

indicators.note: in a down clue, over signals the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a law is a command or rule
a pole is a post

explanation.surface: A politician seizes a military command post.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Robert Walpole was the first British prime minister, a political leader.

clue.text: Chap conceals new name for strong fabric

indicators.note: conceals means the chap's word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a guy is a chap

explanation.surface: A man hides a new label on some tough material.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunny is coarse jute or hemp cloth used for sacking.

clue.text: Young animal appearing to crawl

explanation.definitionFit: A young deer, and also a verb for behaving with servile flattery.

clue.text: Throw so-called writer a flower

parts.note: to lob is to throw underarm or in a high arc
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb, so the writer is only so called

explanation.surface: An instruction to toss a bloom to a pseudonymous author.
explanation.walkthrough: Elia is the pseudonym of Charles Lamb, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a garden plant grown for its small blue blooms.

clue.text: Whip boy from part of Spain

definitions.note: an adjective phrase, matching the answer's adjectival use

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip, shortened to cat
Alan is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad from Spain is a whipping boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalan describes someone or something from Catalonia, a region in north-east Spain.

clue.text: Ulster may depend on this

parts.note: an Ulster is a heavy overcoat, which would hang from the thing in question, rather than the province of Northern Ireland relying on it

explanation.surface: A political remark about what Northern Ireland relies on.
explanation.walkthrough: An Ulster is a long heavy overcoat; 'depend' is used in its literal sense of hang down.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardrobe frame that garments hang from, so an overcoat literally hangs from it.

clue.text: Oldster put in confused state by young beginner?

parts.note: being in a fog is being confused

indicators.note: the beginner of a word is its opening letter, here of the word young

explanation.surface: An elderly person is bewildered by a youthful novice.
explanation.definitionFit: A fogy is an old-fashioned person, typically elderly, set in their ways.

clue.text: Game with staff that comes to a striking end

definitions.text: that comes to a striking end
definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the noun it describes

parts.note: a match is a game
a stick is a staff

explanation.surface: A sports fixture with a cane that finishes dramatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' is literal: the head of the object is struck to light it.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchstick has a head at one end that ignites when rubbed against a rough surface.

clue.text: Supporter' gives -team-leader money demanded

indicators.note: the leader of the word team is the letter at its front

parts.note: a ransom is money demanded for release of a captive

explanation.surface: A backer gives a team captain the cash being asked for.
explanation.walkthrough: A transom is a horizontal beam, so a supporter in the structural sense, not a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a crossbar or beam that bears weight over a door or window.

clue.text: A decoration being worn in my wedding

indicators.note: in says the other pieces sit inside the word my

parts.note: trim is decoration on clothing
clothes on the body are on

explanation.surface: Someone wears a decoration at their own wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A, TRIM and ON inside MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Matrimony is the state of marriage, entered at a wedding.

clue.text: House on the avenue unopened — so we hear from Jack

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the other piece
unopened means the opening letter of the phrase is taken away

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor reports what he hears about a house on an unopened street.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is a sailor (Jack Tar); the answer is the cry sailors chant when hauling.
explanation.definitionFit: Heave-ho is the shout of sailors hauling on a rope, so what you hear from a seaman.

clue.text: One composer frequently listened to another

indicators.note: listened to means the word is heard, pronounced without its t

parts.note: often means frequently
another composer, Bach

explanation.surface: A music lover regularly listens to a second composer.
explanation.walkthrough: OFTEN is commonly said without its T, giving OFFEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Offenbach was a French-German composer of operettas.

clue.text: Allow in again to study at American university

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A student is let back in to study at an American college.
explanation.definitionFit: To readmit is to let someone back in, admitting them a second time.

clue.text: The pound he owed was of vital importance

definitions.text: The pound he owed was of vital importance

parts.words: The pound he owed was of vital importance
parts.note: the pound is a pound of flesh, the bond in The Merchant of Venice, cut from near the heart

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's merchant of Venice borrows from Shylock with a pound of his flesh as security.

clue.text: Record as present, and reprimand

definitions.meaning: to mark a name on a register with a check mark
to scold or tell someone off

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: marking a list with a check, and telling someone off sharply.

clue.text: Working effectively as an artist in free time

indicators.note: in says the artist goes inside the word for free

parts.note: open means free, unrestricted
RA, Royal Academician, is an artist

explanation.surface: A painter keeps working in his spare time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts RA inside OPEN, then T follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Operant means producing effects, active or functioning.

clue.text: Quickly write a dance

parts.note: to jot is to write something down quickly

explanation.surface: An instruction to scribble down a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The jota is a lively folk dance from northern Spain.

clue.text: Con man who disguised how smooth he was

definitions.text: Con man who disguised how smooth he was

parts.words: Con man who disguised how smooth he was
parts.note: the Genesis trickster who covered his smooth skin with goatskins to pass as his hairy brother Esau

explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Jacob deceived his blind father Isaac by posing as his hairy twin to steal the blessing.

clue.text: Male with unusually wide behind from central-region

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the word wide come in an unusual order

parts.note: the stern is the rear part of a ship, so behind

explanation.surface: A man from the heartland is mocked for his unusually broad backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Midwestern describes the central region of the United States.

clue.text: Yarns of the type one might hear from a boxer

definitions.meaning: threads woven across a loom, the weft

definitions.text: of the type one might hear from a boxer
definitions.meaning: the bark of a boxer dog

explanation.definitionFit: Woof is the weft threads in weaving, and also a dog's bark.

clue.text: Journey starts in the river and ends in the creek

indicators.note: starts in means the opening letters of these two words
ends in means the closing letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A journey beginning on the river and finishing in a creek.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is a long, arduous journey.

clue.text: Study book with -port .or with spirit

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port, shortened to Rio

explanation.surface: Someone choosing between reading with port wine or with liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' is a harbour city, not the wine; 'or' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Con brio is an Italian musical direction meaning vigorously or energetically.

clue.text: Island that's all right, in a way? Not quite

parts.note: OK means all right
taken as written

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short of completion, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before being cut short

explanation.surface: A doubtful remark that an island is sort of fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Okinawa is the main island of a chain in southern Japan.

clue.text: Bear left by New York, returning to this district?

parts.note: to brook is to bear or tolerate

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A bear departs from New York and later comes back to this neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' is the verb tolerate, not the animal; 'returning' turns NY into YN.
explanation.definitionFit: Brooklyn is one of the boroughs of New York City, a fitting area given the surface.

clue.text: Point to person who executed quick work

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point
Jack Ketch was a notorious English hangman of the 17th century

explanation.surface: Pointing out the person who carried out a speedy job.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Ketch was a notorious executioner under Charles II, so 'executed' means put to death, not carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing or piece done rapidly.
